messages.subject: Imposing Correlation between endogenous variables
parts:
Hello Everyone

I hope you are enjoying your time.
I have a question which is in my head a few weeks.
If you are familiar with Amos, you would have noticed that it is NOT possible to put a correlation "between two endogenous variable" OR "between an endogenous variable and an exogenous variable" . Correlation is only allowed for exogenous variables.
But this is not the exact case in R, lavaan. You can simply put correlation between two endogenous variable.
Can anyone explain this problem to me? Why you can not do the same in Amos ?

I am grateful for this group and for your answers.

Bests
Afshin

messages.author: 5abdb409f213d464
messages.subject: Re: Imposing Correlation between endogenous variables
parts:
It is true that Amos correlates exogenous variables with a curved arrow. For endogenous variables this happens by correlating the residual variables with a curved arrow. lavaan does the same: http://lavaan.ugent.be/tutorial/syntax1.html
It may be confusing that only one operator exists. Amis is a graphical user interface and lavaan usessyntax. Still, the same thing is modeled.

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Imposing Correlation between endogenous variables
parts: if I remember correctly you don't put the correlation between the variables themselves, but between their errors.
That is correct, but the lavaan syntax is written such that an endogenous variable's residual is identified using the name of the variable itself.
If you are familiar with Amos, you would have noticed that it is NOT possible to put a correlation "between two endogenous variable" OR "between an endogenous variable and an exogenous variable" .

Perhaps by default, but you should be allowed to estimate off-diagonal elements of the theta_epsilon matrix in Amos.  If Amos uses the full LISREL representation, in which case indicators of exogenous and endogenous factors are in different matrices, then that is the practical limitation that prevents correlating indicators of endogenous and exogenous factors.  But to be clear, all indicators are themselves endogenous (they are explained by the latent factors).
But this is not the exact case in R, lavaan. You can simply put correlation between two endogenous variable.

Correct.  And you can correlate any exogenous variables with the residuals of any endogenous variables.  This is because lavaan (like Mplus) uses only the "y side" of the LISREL representation.
